title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is axiomatizing an 'atlas' A = (𝔉, ≤, ≪), the combinatorial skeleton of a tame or stratified topology. 𝔉 is a set of 'figures'. M is the set of strata. ≤ is the closure (face) order on strata, and ≪ is refinement. Each figure F has a 'déploiement' F̃ = M_{≤F}, the poset of its strata.

(1) End of page 13's discussion. A finite poset S is a 'combinatorial simplex' if S ≅ 𝔓*(J), the poset of nonempty subsets of a finite set J. Grothendieck finishes an inductive argument: every element is the sup of the minimal elements it majorizes (with an uncertain correction to 'l'un des'). Taking J to be the set of minimal elements then gives S ≅ 𝔓*(J). This is offered as proof of the page-13 claim: S is a simplex iff S is finite, polyideal, has a greatest element, and every non-minimal element has at least two maximal predecessors.

(2) Definitions. A figure F is (combinatorially) simplicial if F̃ is simplicial. That means F̃ is polyideal and every lower set F̃_{≤X} is a combinatorial simplex. An atlas is simplicial if all its figures are. Every lower interval being Boolean is exactly the modern notion of a simplicial poset.

(3) He then weakens the polyideality axiom 'At pol 1'. For his purposes it suffices to assume Axiome 1: for every X ∈ M, the boundary ∂X = {Y ∈ M | Y < X} is either empty (X minimal) or has at least two maximal elements. This is a necessary condition for face posets of regular CW complexes. There, ∂X is a regular cell decomposition of a sphere S^{n-1}, which needs at least two top cells. It excludes things like a 2-cell attached by a loop made of one vertex and one edge.

(4) Axiom C, a 'criterion of compatibility of refinements of subfigures'. Take strata X, Y with refinements X' ≪ X and Y' ≪ Y. Suppose X and Y are compatible (barred-≍ symbol: sub-figures of a common figure). Let L = X ∩ Y = {Z | Z ≤ X, Y}. Let X'_L = X'.L = {X'' ∈ X̃' | X'' ≪ L} be the refinement of L induced by X', and similarly Y'_L.
- Already known: X' compatible with Y' implies X'_L compatible with Y'_L.
- The axiom asserts the converse: X'_L compatible with Y'_L implies X' compatible with Y'.

Purpose: the axiom is designed to make the following proposition valid. For figures F' ≪ F and G' ≪ G with F, G sub-figures of H, and L = F ∩ G, refinements F' and G' are compatible iff their restrictions to L are. This is a local-to-global (sheaf/gluing) principle. Refinements of two subfigures glue to a refinement of F ∪ G iff they agree on the overlap. Page 15 interprets it via cartesian squares of 'Ombres' (supports) and of déploiements. Compatibility need only be tested on strata X' ≪ L and Y' ≪ L.

The PL analogue is standard: subdivisions of subcomplexes K1, K2 that agree on K1 ∩ K2 glue to a subdivision of K1 ∪ K2. Grothendieck promotes this to an axiom of his abstract tame-topology framework.
errors: The characterization of combinatorial simplices used here (finite + polyideal + greatest element + every non-minimal element has at least two maximal predecessors implies S ≅ 𝔓*(J)) is false as stated. Counterexample: the face poset of a square (one top element T, four edges a=xy, b=yz, c=zw, d=wx, four vertices). Pairs with a common lower bound have an inf, T is greatest, and every non-minimal element has at least two maximal predecessors. Every element is even the sup of the minimal elements below it. Yet the poset has 9 elements, while 𝔓*({x,y,z,w}) has 15. The inductive step 'S ≅ 𝔓*(J)' fails because polyideality does not force all subsets of minimal elements to have distinct sups. A correct criterion needs each lower interval to be Boolean, e.g. an element of height k has exactly k+1 atoms below it.
The 'Inj''(X, L)' in the definition of X'_L should presumably involve X' (the refined figure), not X: X'_L = {X'' ∈ X̃' | X'' ≪ L}. This is a slip of notation.

Axiom 1 alone (at least two maximal boundary strata) does not recover polyideality or simpliciality. Grothendieck explicitly says it suffices for his needs, so this is not an error, but it is much weaker than At pol 1.

ideas.what: Poset in which every lower set M_{≤X} is a combinatorial simplex 𝔓*(J) ('ensemble ordonné simplicial'; simplicial figure/atlas)
Polyideal poset: pairs with a common lower bound have an inf; self-dual reformulation
ideas.modern_name: locally meet-semilattice / poset with meets of bounded-below pairs (cf. 'simplicial complex'-type face posets)

ideas.what: Axiome 1: the boundary ∂X of any non-minimal stratum has at least two maximal elements
ideas.modern_name: necessary condition for CW posets / regular CW face posets (boundary is a sphere, which needs at least two top cells); related to 'thinness'

ideas.what: Axiom C: compatibility of refinements of two subfigures is detected on their intersection (gluing of refinements)
ideas.modern_name: gluing of subdivisions / sheaf-like property of refinements in tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in PL topology (gluing subdivisions agreeing on subcomplexes); no axiomatic version credited
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 only sketches 'topologie modérée' without these axioms

missed.claim: An axiomatic, purely combinatorial framework for tame topology: atlases of figures with a face order ≤ and a refinement relation ≪, plus axioms such as Axiom 1 and the refinement-gluing Axiom C. It is meant to recover cartesian squares of supports ('Ombres') and déploiements. This program, announced vaguely in the Esquisse, was never developed or published, and later o-minimal or stratified approaches do not phrase gluing of refinements as an axiom on such a structure.
missed.quote: Ax C (Critère de compatibilité des raffinements des sous-figures) ... Alors X'_L ≍ Y'_L ⇒ X' ≍ Y'.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could inform combinatorial or synthetic foundations of stratified spaces: exit-path categories, constructible sheaves, and poset-stratified spaces in the style of Lurie or Ayala-Francis-Tanaka. There, gluing of refinements is usually handled ad hoc.

missed.claim: Independent formulation, in 1986, of simplicial posets and of a CW-poset-type boundary condition inside a tame-topology axiomatics. This connects Grothendieck's analysis situs to the combinatorics of Björner and Stanley, which developed in parallel.
missed.quote: ∂X = {Y ∈ M | Y < X} est vide ... ou admet au moins deux éléments maximaux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical interest; it shows Grothendieck converging on face-poset combinatorics as the backbone of his 'topologie modérée'.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains standard combinatorial notions (simplicial posets, a CW-type boundary condition) and a natural gluing axiom for refinements. It documents an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology program, but nothing a specialist would find mathematically startling. The simplex characterization carried over from page 13 is actually flawed.
transcription_corrections: 'si elle est polyédrale' should read 'si elle est polyidéale' (consistent with page 13's definitions).
'Une stratification[?] est dite (combinatoirement) simpliciale' is more likely 'Un atlas est dit (combinatoirement) simplicial si toutes ses figures sont simpliciales'.

'Axiome 1' is written 'Ax[iome] 1'. The struck passage reads roughly 'si X n'est pas minimal ... l'ens X̃ = M_{≤X} est un simplexe combinatoire ... dans (M,≤), alors X a au moins deux éléments prédécesseurs maximaux'.
The relation symbol rendered ≍ in 'X ≍ Y', 'F ≍ G', 'X'_L ≍ Y'_L' is a barred ≍ in the manuscript. It denotes compatibility (sub-figures of a common figure), not its negation.
Section heading 'Ax C' appears as 'At C' or 'Ax C' (axiome C), with 'Axiome' struck and replaced by 'Critère'. '(∈ M)' is an interlinear insertion after X, Y, X', Y'.
'Inj''(X, L)': the argument is probably X' (refined figure), possibly a slip in the manuscript itself.
